greek: εἶπεν δὲ κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν Εἰπὸν Ααρων τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου Ἔκτεινον τῇ χειρὶ τὴν ῥάβδον σου ἐπὶ τοὺς ποταμοὺς καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς διώρυγας καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἕλη καὶ ἀνάγαγε τοὺς βατράχους.
hint: The lord tells Moses to have Aaron stretch out his rod over the rivers, canals and marshes and bring up the frogs.

notes.text: Rahlfs numbers 8:1–28 as the Hebrew does; many English Bibles number them 8:5–32.

(Ααρων, from Hebrew ʾAhărōn, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἐξέτεινεν Ααρων τὴν χεῖρα ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα Αἰγύπτου καὶ ἀνήγαγεν τοὺς βατράχους· καὶ ἀνεβιβάσθη ὁ βάτραχος καὶ ἐκάλυψεν τὴν γῆν Αἰγύπτου.
hint: Aaron stretches out his hand over Egypt's waters; the frogs come up and cover the land.

notes.text: The frog, singular and collective, for the Hebrew haṣṣĕpardēaʿ, also singular.

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: ἐποίησαν δὲ ὡσαύτως καὶ οἱ ἐπαοιδοὶ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ταῖς φαρμακείαις αὐτῶν καὶ ἀνήγαγον τοὺς βατράχους ἐπὶ γῆν Αἰγύπτου.
hint: The Egyptian enchanters do the same with their sorceries and bring up frogs on the land.

notes.text: They brought up: the enchanters add frogs, and remove none.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Φαραω Μωυσῆν καὶ Ααρων καὶ εἶπεν Εὔξασθε περὶ ἐμοῦ πρὸς κύριον, καὶ περιελέτω τοὺς βατράχους ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ ἐξαποστελῶ τὸν λαόν, καὶ θύσωσιν κυρίῳ.
hint: Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron, asks them to pray for the frogs' removal, and promises to release the people.

notes.text: ἐμοῦ between the article and its noun is the possessive ἐμός, my, not the pronoun.
And they may sacrifice to the lord: the subjunctive of purpose after the promise.

hint: Moses asks Pharaoh to set the time for his prayer that the frogs be removed, except those in the river.

notes.text: Set for me: the Hebrew has hitpāʾēr ʿālay, have the glory over me.

greek: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ ἐπαοιδοὶ τῷ Φαραω Δάκτυλος θεοῦ ἐστιν τοῦτο. καὶ ἐσκληρύνθη ἡ καρδία Φαραω, καὶ οὐκ εἰσήκουσεν αὐτῶν, καθάπερ ἐλάλησεν κύριος.
hint: The enchanters tell Pharaoh it is the finger of God; his heart is hardened and he does not listen.

notes.text: The finger of God, θεοῦ without the article, for the Hebrew ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm. Luke 11:20 has ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ.

hint: Moses is to rise early, stand before Pharaoh at the water, and demand the people's release.

notes.text: In the desert: not in the Hebrew of this verse.

greek: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ βούλῃ ἐξαποστεῖλαι τὸν λαόν μου, ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐπαποστέλλω ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς θεράποντάς σου καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν λαόν σου καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς οἴκους ὑμῶν κυνόμυιαν, καὶ πλησθήσονται αἱ οἰκίαι τῶν Αἰγυπτίων τῆς κυνομυίης καὶ εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἐφʼ ἧς εἰσιν ἐπʼ αὐτῆς.
hint: If Pharaoh refuses, the lord will send dog-flies on him and his people, filling Egypt's houses and land.

notes.text: κυνόμυια, the dog-fly, filed under κυνάμυια, 'shameless fly': the Hebrew has ʿārōb, a swarm, of uncertain kind.
The relative and then the pronoun again.

greek: καὶ παραδοξάσω ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τὴν γῆν Γεσεμ, ἐφʼ ἧς ὁ λαός μου ἔπεστιν ἐπʼ αὐτῆς, ἐφʼ ἧς οὐκ ἔσται ἐκεῖ ἡ κυνόμυια, ἵνα εἰδῇς ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι κύριος ὁ κύριος πάσης τῆς γῆς·
hint: The land of Goshen, where the lord's people live, will be set apart and have no flies.

greek: καὶ δώσω διαστολὴν ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ἐμοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σοῦ λαοῦ· ἐν δὲ τῇ αὔριον ἔσται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The lord will set a distinction between his people and Pharaoh's; the sign will come tomorrow.

notes.text: διαστολή, a notch, a distinction, for the Hebrew pĕdut, redemption, which the Greek reads as division.

hint: Moses leaves Pharaoh and prays.

notes.text: To God: the Hebrew has ʾel-YHWH.

reading: [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Μωυσῆς]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of [[name:Φαραω]] and [[prayed|prayed, offered prayers, paid his vows, made a vow, prayed for|εὔχομαι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]];

greek: ἐποίησεν δὲ κύριος καθάπερ εἶπεν Μωυσῆς, καὶ περιεῖλεν τὴν κυνόμυιαν ἀπὸ Φαραω καὶ τῶν θεραπόντων αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐ κατελείφθη οὐδεμία.
hint: The lord removes the flies from Pharaoh, his servants and his people, and not one is left.

notes.text: Not one, feminine, agreeing with κυνόμυια.

reading: [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[according as|according as and just as, like as if and exactly as|καθάπερ]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]], and [[took off something that surrounds|took off something that surrounds and took off an outer coat and took away and stripped off|περιαιρέω]] [[the dog-fly|the dog-fly, the shameless fly|κυνόμυια]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of [[name:Φαραω]] and [[of the waiting-men|of the waiting-men and attendants, of the companions in arms, of the servants|θεράπων]] of him and [[of the people|of the people, of the men, of the soldiers, of the land-army, of the common men, of the folk, of the Jews, of the Christians|λαός]] of him, and not [[was left behind|was left behind, was left as an heritage, was forsaken and abandoned and left in the lurch, was left remaining, was left alone|καταλείπω]] [[and not one|and not one, no one and none, naught and good for naught|οὐδείς]].

greek: καὶ ἐβάρυνεν Φαραω τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ καιροῦ τούτου καὶ οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἐξαποστεῖλαι τὸν λαόν.
hint: Pharaoh hardens his heart this time too and refuses to release the people.

notes.text: Also at this time: καί the adverb, for the Hebrew gam bappaʿam hazzōʾt.
βαρύνω, active: he weighed down his heart.

reading: and [[weighed down|weighed down and oppressed by weight and depressed, oppressed and wearied|βαρύνω]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[the heart|the heart, the stomach|καρδία]] of him [[also|also and even, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the due measure|of the due measure and proportion and fitness, of the vital part, of the right point of time, of the proper time and season, of the exact and critical time, of the time, of the advantage and profit and fruit|καιρός]] [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]] and not [[willed|willed, wished, purposed, was wont and accustomed, meant and purported|θέλω]] [[to send quite away|to send quite away, to dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]].
